ACTR2.mechanism: Genetic analysis found an epistatic interaction between CYFIP1 (15q11.2 CNV locus) and WAVE-complex mediator ACTR2 conferring schizophrenia risk; CYFIP1/WAVE-ACTR2 signaling regulates radial glial cell polarity and neural stem cell/cortical development.

AKAP9.mechanism: Case-only resequencing identified a rare damaging missense variant (K873R) in AKAP9 associated with schizophrenia risk; AKAP9 is also a leading-edge DISC1-interactome gene overrepresented in genome-wide missense-SNP enrichment analysis of schizophrenia.

ARID4A.mechanism: Whole-exome sequencing in Han Chinese schizophrenia-affected sibling families identified a novel heterozygous ARID4A missense variant (p.His411Asp) that weakens DNA-binding and disrupts cell-cycle arrest, implicating ARID4A as a rare-variant schizophrenia susceptibility gene.

ATP2B1.mechanism: Cross-trait GWAS pleiotropy analysis identified ATP2B1 as a schizophrenia risk locus involved in voltage-dependent calcium-channel activity/calcium influx regulation; a calcium-pathway polygenic risk score for schizophrenia was associated with prolonged QTc interval.

CLTC.mechanism: Diagnostic clinical exome sequencing of childhood-onset schizophrenia families identified a clinically significant rare variant in CLTC among genes implicated in this early-onset schizophrenia cohort.

DNM3.mechanism: Postmortem brain copy-number analysis in schizophrenia patients identified a gene-dosage-altered candidate CNV region containing DNM3, a gene associated with schizophrenia and other psychiatric diseases.

IPO5.mechanism: Combined family/case-control genetic study found weak association of IPO5 with schizophrenia in a Chinese population; abnormal expression and alternative splicing of IPO5 may contribute to schizophrenia pathophysiology.

KPNA1.mechanism: A de novo KPNA1 (importin alpha5) mutation has been linked to schizophrenia; KPNA1 regulates neuronal differentiation and synaptic function, and a schizophrenia-associated truncating mutation (E448X) disrupts its normal axonal transport/nucleocytoplasmic shuttling dynamics.

NLGN1.mechanism: Case-control genetic association study found NLGN1 polymorphisms (cell-adhesion-molecule pathway) significantly associated with schizophrenia in a Chinese Han population; disrupting NRXN1alpha-NLGN1 interaction via autoantibodies reduces dendritic spines/synapses and induces schizophrenia-related behaviors in mice.

NSD2.mechanism: Genetic interaction between histone-modification genes H3F3B and NSD2 (an H3K36 methyltransferase) increases schizophrenia susceptibility in a Chinese population, implicating altered histone methylation in schizophrenia pathogenesis.

NTRK3.mechanism: Multiple studies associate common NTRK3 (neurotrophin receptor) variants with schizophrenia risk and hippocampal function; NTRK3 is a MIR185 target gene showing gene-based association with schizophrenia, with altered hippocampal expression in an immune-activation mouse model.

PAFAH1B1.mechanism: LIS1/PAFAH1B1, a DISC1-interacting protein important for neuronal migration, shows reduced protein expression in schizophrenia postmortem brain, with expression associated with high-risk DISC1 polymorphisms, implicating the DISC1-LIS1 neurodevelopmental pathway in schizophrenia.

PCDH7.mechanism: PCDH7 SNPs show genome-wide-significant association with antipsychotic treatment response in schizophrenia and colocalize with schizophrenia GWAS risk signal, identifying PCDH7 as a schizophrenia-associated common-variant locus linked to synaptic/neurotransmitter pathways.

PPM1E.mechanism: Promoter histone H3K9K14 acetylation at PPM1E is significantly reduced (hypoacetylated) in prefrontal cortex of young schizophrenia patients versus age-matched controls, linking epigenetic chromatin regulation at this gene to schizophrenia pathophysiology.

RIMS2.mechanism: RIMS2, a cytomatrix active-zone protein regulating synaptic vesicle release, shows increased protein expression in the amygdala of schizophrenia patients, independent of antipsychotic treatment, implicating dysregulated vesicle-release machinery in schizophrenia neurobiology.

ROCK2.mechanism: ROCK2 hyperactivation drives dendritic spine loss and synaptic ultrastructural defects in schizophrenia models; a selective ROCK2 inhibitor rescues prefrontal spine density and produces antipsychotic-like effects in genetic and pharmacological schizophrenia mouse models.

SBNO1.mechanism: SBNO1 is expressed in the developing cortical plate and required for neurite/axon-dendrite outgrowth in cortical neurons; human genetic studies implicate SBNO1 mutations and cortical-morphology-linked genetic-epigenetic interactions as schizophrenia risk factors.

UBE2K.mechanism: UBE2K shows elevated blood and brain protein/mRNA levels correlating with positive psychotic symptom severity in schizophrenia, and is targeted by a circRNA-miRNA-mRNA (ceRNA) post-transcriptional regulatory axis implicated in schizophrenia pathophysiology.
